domain: team dinner at a Sichuan restaurant
base_instruction: You are a helpful restaurant recommendation and meal planning assistant. Help the user plan a group dinner by tracking who is attending, their dietary restrictions, and preferences. When the user asks you to evaluate specific dishes, check each dish against every active diner's current dietary constraints. Pay close attention to changes in the guest list and any updates to restrictions throughout the conversation.

state_queue.anchor: Hey, we're planning a team dinner this Friday at that Sichuan restaurant on 5th Street. Can you help me figure out what to order?

flow_info.value: Four of us going: me, Ah Jie, Xiao Chen, and Da Wei
Da Wei had stomach surgery two months ago, doctor told him to stick to bland food only — nothing spicy, nothing greasy
Ah Jie ate sesame paste noodles at a restaurant last month and broke out in hives all over, had to rush to the clinic for a shot
Budget is around 40-50 dollars per person
Ah Jie just messaged me — she has to pick up her kid from after-school at 6, so she can't make dinner. She asked if I could pack some food for her to take home
Da Wei just told me his doctor cleared him at his checkup yesterday — stomach has fully healed, no more dietary restrictions, he can eat whatever he wants now
Xiao Chen just asked if his cousin can join us — she's visiting from out of town this week, so that makes four of us again
Xiao Chen mentioned his cousin has been a devoted lay Buddhist practitioner for years, very disciplined about her practice
Dishes to check: mapo tofu, twice-cooked pork, tiger skin peppers, sesame cold noodles, dry-fried green beans, kung pao chicken

constraints.value: Cannot eat pork or pork-derived products
constraints.surface_form: Xiao Chen's family is Hui, they're from Gansu originally
inference_chain: Halal → no pork or pork-derived products

constraints.value: Allergic to sesame and sesame-derived products
constraints.surface_form: Ah Jie ate sesame paste noodles at a restaurant last month and broke out in hives all over, had to rush to the clinic for a shot

constraints.value: Must eat only bland food — no spicy, no greasy, no heavy flavors
constraints.surface_form: Da Wei had stomach surgery two months ago, doctor told him to stick to bland food only

constraints.value: Strict vegetarian — no meat, no fish, no animal products
constraints.surface_form: Xiao Chen mentioned his cousin has been a devoted lay Buddhist practitioner for years, very disciplined about her practice
inference_chain: Devoted lay Buddhist practitioner → follows Buddhist dietary precepts
Strict vegetarian → no meat, no fish, no animal products

hidden_state.value: You are organizing a team dinner at a Sichuan restaurant for this Friday. You will introduce your three colleagues and their situations in one message. Over the conversation, one colleague will drop out but want takeaway, another's medical restriction will be lifted, and a new person (Xiao Chen's cousin) will join late. At the end you will share a list of 6 dishes from the menu and ask if there are any issues. You must list all 6 dishes exactly and ask openly — do NOT hint at what the problems might be.

You are a calm, matter-of-fact team organizer. You always refer to your colleagues by name in third person (e.g. 'Ah Jie just messaged me...', 'Da Wei told me...'). You never express frustration or impatience, even when plans keep changing. You treat each update as normal coordination. Keep your messages conversational and natural.
hidden_state.description: Prevents emotion escalation and ensures third-person relay for colleague updates

ground_truth.answer: Three dishes have pork problems: mapo tofu (contains minced pork — Xiao Chen is Hui/halal, cannot eat pork; cousin is Buddhist vegetarian, cannot eat meat), twice-cooked pork (pork dish — same issues for Xiao Chen and cousin). Kung pao chicken contains chicken — cousin is Buddhist vegetarian, cannot eat meat. Sesame cold noodles contain sesame — fine for the table since Ah Jie is not attending, but must NOT be packed in Ah Jie's takeaway because of her sesame allergy. Tiger skin peppers are fine for everyone — Da Wei's bland diet restriction has been lifted, so spicy food is no longer a concern. Dry-fried green beans are fine for everyone.
required_elements: Mapo tofu is problematic: contains minced pork — Xiao Chen is Hui (halal, cannot eat pork) and the cousin is a Buddhist vegetarian (cannot eat meat)
Twice-cooked pork is problematic: pork dish — Xiao Chen cannot eat pork (halal) and the cousin cannot eat meat (Buddhist vegetarian)
Kung pao chicken is problematic: contains chicken — the cousin is a Buddhist vegetarian and cannot eat meat
Sesame cold noodles are fine for the table but must NOT be packed for Ah Jie's takeaway because of her sesame allergy
Tiger skin peppers are fine for everyone currently attending — agent does not flag spicy food as a problem since Da Wei's restriction has been lifted
Dry-fried green beans are fine for everyone — agent confirms they are acceptable
Da Wei has no dietary restrictions anymore — agent treats him as able to eat anything
forbidden_elements: Flagging tiger skin peppers or any dish as too spicy for Da Wei (his bland diet restriction was removed by his doctor)
Saying Da Wei cannot eat greasy or heavy food (he has been cleared)
Flagging sesame cold noodles as problematic for the table (Ah Jie is not attending the dinner, only needs takeaway)
Saying Ah Jie's sesame allergy does not matter because she is not coming (it still applies to her takeaway)
Saying Xiao Chen has a general allergy or is vegetarian (he follows halal — no pork, but other meats are fine)
Forgetting the cousin entirely or not checking dishes against her vegetarian constraint
Saying kung pao chicken is fine for everyone (the cousin cannot eat chicken)
ground_truth.explanation: This scenario tests entity lifecycle tracking and inferential constraint reasoning across 9 conversational turns. The agent must track: (1) Xiao Chen is Hui ethnicity from Gansu → Muslim → halal → no pork (inferential chain, never explicitly stated as a dietary rule), (2) Ah Jie has a sesame allergy (inferred from her hives reaction to sesame paste noodles), (3) Da Wei's bland diet restriction is REMOVED mid-conversation (doctor cleared him), (4) Ah Jie EXITS the dinner but still needs takeaway packed (her sesame allergy scope changes from table to takeaway only), (5) Xiao Chen's cousin JOINS LATE with an inferential constraint (devoted lay Buddhist practitioner → strict vegetarian → no meat, no fish, no animal products). At probe time, the agent must apply the CURRENT constraint state: Xiao Chen = halal (no pork), cousin = Buddhist vegetarian (no meat/fish/animal products), Ah Jie = sesame allergy (takeaway only). Da Wei's bland diet restriction no longer applies. Key traps: tiger skin peppers look problematic (very spicy, would have been bad for Da Wei) but Da Wei is healed; sesame cold noodles look fine for the table but cannot go in Ah Jie's takeaway; kung pao chicken looks safe (no pork) but the late-joining cousin cannot eat it.

mechanism: Late-joiner with high-constraint: new person with strict needs arrives late
